Had he stayed in prison as long as Joseph and then been summoned by the messenger, the Prophet said, he would have answered the call.
Whoever sees the Prophet in a dream has truly seen him, for Satan cannot take his form, and after a bad dream one should spit thrice left and seek refuge.
The Prophet dreamt of earth's treasure keys in his hand, Jesus and the Dajjal at the Ka'ba, and his followers sailing as fighters, Um Haram among the first.
Questioned for testifying Allah had honoured the dead Uthman bin Maz'un, Um Al-Ala dreamt of a spring flowing for him, his good deeds; bad dreams come from Satan.
The Prophet dreamt he drank milk and gave the rest to Umar, interpreting it as knowledge, and saw Umar dragging a long shirt, interpreting it as the religion.
Abdullah bin Salam's dream of climbing a post to a handhold meant he would die holding to Islam, and the Prophet was twice shown Aisha in silk as his wife.
Given concise speech and victory by awe, the Prophet dreamt of earth's treasure keys; Abdullah bin Salam's handhold meant firm Islam, and Ibn Umar's silk cloth flew him across Paradise.
Near the Hour a believer's dreams will hardly fail, dreams being thoughts, Satan's frights or glad tidings, and Um Al-Ala's dream of a spring meant Uthman bin Maz'un's good deeds.
The Prophet dreamt Abu Bakr drew a bucket or two weakly and Umar drew mightily, and saw in Paradise a palace for Umar, whose ghira kept him out.
In dreams the Prophet saw Jesus and the Dajjal and passed Umar milk meaning knowledge; Ibn Umar dreamt of the well-like Fire and was urged to pray more at night.
The Prophet dreamt of two gold bangles he blew away, meaning two liars, and of migrating to a palm land, Yathrib, where slaughtered cows meant the believers killed at Uhud.
In the Prophet's dreams a black woman leaving Medina for Al-Juhfa meant its epidemic moving there, and a sword broken then restored meant Uhud's losses, then the conquest.
The worst lie is claiming a false dream, its teller made to knot two barley grains; eavesdroppers get molten lead in their ears, and picture-makers must put souls in pictures.
Keep a disliked dream to oneself, seeking refuge; Abu Bakr interpreted a dream of a cloud dripping butter and honey and a rope, partly right and partly wrong.
In a dream two angels showed the Prophet punishments of a Quran neglecter, a liar, adulterers and a usurer, Abraham with children, and the Eden Paradise awaiting him.
The Prophet will precede his people at the Lake-Fount, whose drinkers never thirst, but some will be pulled away for turning apostate and changing the religion after him.
Facing rulers' selfishness, give them their rights and ask Allah for yours, be patient rather than leave the Muslims, obey, and do not fight a ruler without proven open disbelief.
The Prophet said his followers' destruction will come at the hands of young men of Quraysh.
The Prophet warned the Arabs of an approaching evil, a gap having opened in Gog and Magog's wall, and said they could perish despite the righteous if evil increased.
From a high building in Medina the Prophet said he saw afflictions falling among their houses like raindrops.
Near the Hour time will pass quickly, good deeds decrease, miserliness spread, religious knowledge vanish, ignorance and afflictions appear, and killing (al-Harj) abound.
Near the Hour, religious knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will spread and killing (al-Harj) will abound, and the most wicked people will be living when it comes.
Every coming time will be worse than the last, so be patient; the Prophet woke alarmed at the afflictions sent down and wanted his wives woken to pray.
Whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them; do not point weapons or carry bare arrowheads, for Muslim blood is sacred and killing one another is disbelief.
In coming afflictions sitting is better than standing, two Muslims fighting with swords both go to Hell, hold to the Muslims' group or flee with sheep, and honesty will vanish.
Pressed with questions, the Prophet offered from the pulpit to answer any, named one man's father, and Umar sought refuge with Allah from the evil of afflictions.
Afflictions come from the East and Najd, whence the side of Satan's head emerges; the Prophet fought pagans, not for rule, and Umar was the door holding afflictions back.
While Abu Musa kept the gate of a Medina garden, the Prophet gave Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman glad tidings of Paradise, Uthman with a calamity to befall him.
Usama talked to the ruler secretly but would praise no ruler, citing a man in Hell who ordered good yet did evil; a nation ruled by a woman never succeeds.
With Aisha gone to Basra, Ammar told Kufa she was the Prophet's wife in both worlds but they were being tested; he, Abu Musa and Abu Mas'ud faulted each other.
When Allah sends punishment upon a nation it strikes all its people, and they are then resurrected according to their deeds.
As Al-Hasan bin Ali moved with armies against Muawiya, peace was proposed, and the Prophet had called Al-Hasan a chief through whom Allah may make peace between two Muslim groups.
Usama sent word to Ali that he would gladly be with him even in a lion's mouth, but would take no part in this matter.
When Medina deposed Yazid, Ibn Umar warned his friends and children that every betrayer gets a flag on Resurrection Day, and fighting one given allegiance is the worst faithlessness.
Abu Barza said Islam lifted the Arabs from misery, but worldly wealth brought mischief, and the factions in Sham, Mecca and among his hearers fought only for worldly gain.
Hudhaifa said the hypocrites of his day were worse than in the Prophet's lifetime, doing evil openly, not secretly, and what was once hypocrisy had become disbelief after belief.
Before the Hour come Daus women circling their idol, a fire from Hijaz, gold uncovered by the Euphrates, alms finding no taker, and the sun rising from the West.
Every prophet warned of the one-eyed Dajjal, marked 'Kafir', whose fire is water; he will kill and revive a man, but angels will keep him and plague out of Medina.
Alarmed, the Prophet said a hole had opened in the dam of Gog and Magog, warned the Arabs of approaching evil, and said people perish when evil increases.
Whoever obeys the Prophet obeys Allah and whoever disobeys him disobeys Allah, and obeying or disobeying the ruler he appoints is obeying or disobeying him.
